entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Berthold of Hanover was a German Cistercian and Bishop of Livonia, who met his death in a crusade against the pagan Livonians.

Born around 1160, Berthold was consecrated as Bishop of Livonia in 1177 and played a key role in the Livonian Crusade, a military campaign aimed at Christianizing the region.

The crusade, which began in 1198, was marked by brutal violence and massacres of the local population, resulting in the deaths of thousands of Livonians. Berthold's involvement in the crusade had a lasting impact on the region, leading to the eventual Christianization of Livonia and the establishment of the Hanseatic League.

Despite his significant role in Livonian history, Berthold's legacy has been largely forgotten in modern times, with many historians viewing him as a relic of a bygone era. Nevertheless, his contributions to the Livonian Crusade and the Christianization of Livonia remain an important part of the region's complex and often fraught history.

As a testament to the enduring legacy of the Livonian Crusade, Berthold's name remains etched in the annals of history, serving as a reminder of the devastating consequences of colonialism and the importance of preserving the cultural heritage of indigenous populations.

In the words of the German historian, 'Berthold of Hanover was a product of his time, a man shaped by the brutal realities of the crusade, and his legacy serves as a poignant reminder of the complexities of human history.'
